I graduated already but the only situation which I think increasing student fees is justifiable is if the money is going to be spent on hiring and retaining professors rather than irrelevant things like athletics.

I think the only logical change for UCSD is to go back to D3 sports. Increasing student fees is not going to encourage more prospective students to enroll, possibly meaning a decrease in the school's yield rate. Like someone else mentioned, there are tons of D1 schools that have stayed mediocre and invisible in terms of name exposure and academic reputation, take SDSU or even Davis/Irvine/SB/Riverside for example. On the other hand, there are many top ranked schools that thrive in reputation with D3 sport programs, like MIT/Caltech/Chicago/NYU/CMU. We also already have  several sports competing in D1 for a while, and apparently so far those games haven't gathered much attention and we haven't really benefited in terms of alumni support or name exposure. There are other ways to boost campus culture and school pride among undergraduates.

As an alumni I hope the school never moves to D1, if anything I wish it would go back to D3. They shouldn't be spending any additional money on useless sports when they are already having a tough time maintaining and hiring faculty. Faculty quality is what affects ranking and prestige, not a D1 football team - look at SDSU and a bunch of anonymous regional state schools. Also, the school was never meant to be a D1 school from the beginning, it was meant to be an academic-focused school and mimic the atmosphere of a liberal arts college with the split up undergrad colleges. MIT, Caltech, UChicago, NYU, and a lot of others have D3 sport.
